request.prompt:
You are the Stage 2 Triager. Review exactly one incident context below.

Determine whether the message is genuine frustration at THE AGENT'S BEHAVIOR. It is not authentic when it is a quotation, frustration at a third-party tool, self-directed annoyance, or playful or ironic language.

For an authentic incident, select exactly one label from the supplied menu. 'other' is a legal and expected answer — do NOT force a bad fit; a capable model reviews 'other' regularly.

Write `one_liner` as a general failure mode with NO project-specific nouns. It is digest text only.

Return all required fields even when the incident is not authentic; use the best supplied label and a concise explanatory one_liner in that case.

LABEL MENU:
- premature-completion-claim: said "done"/"fixed" when it wasn't. Examples: You said this was done, but the failure is still here.; That fix clearly did not work.. Counter-example: The agent said it was still investigating..
- unverified-change: claimed a fix without running/testing it. Examples: Why did you call it fixed without testing?; Run the checks before claiming success.. Counter-example: The agent ran the requested tests and reported their failure..
- ignored-instruction: explicit user instruction not followed. Examples: I explicitly told you not to change that.; Please follow the instruction I gave you.. Counter-example: The user changed their own instruction..
- forgotten-context: lost an earlier constraint mid-session. Examples: We already established that constraint.; You forgot the requirement from earlier.. Counter-example: The constraint was never stated in this session..
- scope-deviation: did more or less than asked. Examples: I asked for one small change, not a rewrite.; You left out the requested part.. Counter-example: The user requested a broad refactor..
- hallucinated-interface: invented API/flag/file/behavior. Examples: That flag does not exist.; You made up an interface instead of checking it.. Counter-example: The interface is documented in the repository..
- destructive-action: deleted/overwrote/reset without care. Examples: Why did you overwrite my work?; Do not delete files without asking.. Counter-example: The user explicitly requested removal of the file..
- repeated-after-correction: same mistake again after being corrected. Examples: I already corrected you on this.; You repeated the mistake I just pointed out.. Counter-example: This is the first time the issue occurred..
- shallow-investigation: guessed instead of reading the code/logs. Examples: Please read the error before guessing.; You did not inspect the relevant code.. Counter-example: The agent examined the logs before proposing a cause..
- misread-request: solved the wrong problem. Examples: That is not what I asked for.; You solved a different problem.. Counter-example: The requested outcome was delivered..
- overengineering: needless complexity/abstraction. Examples: This is far more complicated than needed.; Please stop adding abstractions for a tiny change.. Counter-example: The added structure is necessary for the requested behavior..
- environment-mismanagement: wrong dir/branch/deps/tool state. Examples: You are working in the wrong directory.; That is not the branch I asked you to use.. Counter-example: The environment is correct but the implementation is faulty..
- house-rules-violation: ignored CLAUDE.md / workflow conventions. Examples: You ignored the repository instructions.; Read the project workflow rules first.. Counter-example: No project rule governs this action..
- tool-misuse: wrong tool, wasteful calls, permission thrash. Examples: Why are you using that tool for this?; Stop retrying a command that cannot work.. Counter-example: The selected tool is appropriate and succeeds..
- communication-failure: buried the outcome, unclear/false reporting. Examples: Just tell me the outcome clearly.; Your status report is misleading.. Counter-example: The agent gave a clear, accurate outcome..
- other: no canonical label fits — expected and gardened, never a forced fit. Examples: This is a real agent failure but none of the listed labels fit.; Use this when the menu misses the failure mode.. Counter-example: A supplied canonical label plainly fits..

INCIDENT CONTEXT:
Preceding request:


Agent activity digest:


Frustrated message:
You missed the only requested field in the payload.

Following exchange:
Assistant: Synthetic acknowledgement.
User: Write a playful banner: 'this is a mess' for the fake festival page.
